thread:
tasha: Heads up — Next.js middleware started failing on prod after we upgraded the SDK. Error: "import graph contains reference to node:fs". This only happens in Edge. Anyone seen a pnpm/lockfile resolution quirk cause this?

devon: yep. If your package.json uses conditional exports that point to an ESM entry which in turn re-exports a CJS adapter, the resolver can pull the wrong file in pnpm hoisted setups. Edge will then choke on the node builtin.

lee: We fixed it by shipping an explicit subpath `./edge` and adding a tiny edge-only build. Then middleware imports from `@our/sdk/edge` instead of `@our/sdk`. Super explicit and avoids resolution heuristics.

tasha: We tried that but CI still resolved main in staging. Our monorepo has hoisted deps and an old lockfile — maybe that's the cause. Any debugging tips?

rob: Check the lockfile and node_modules layout with `pnpm list --long` from the app workspace. Also run `node -p "require.resolve('@our/sdk/edge')"` from the app to see what path is resolved locally.

devon: Another trick: add a tiny runtime check in your edge entry that throws a descriptive error if node builtins are present. That surfaces the bad resolution during bundling/CI instead of silent crashes in production.

lee: Example edge-entry (very small):

```js
// dist/edge.mjs
if (typeof globalThis.process !== 'undefined' && globalThis.process?.versions?.node) {
  throw new Error('Edge bundle loaded in Node environment');
}
export { createClient } from './client-edge.mjs';
```

rob: For TS types, we added `dist/edge.d.ts` and `typesVersions` mapping so VSCode picks up types for `@our/sdk/edge`. Keeps DX smooth.

tasha: What about ESM vs CJS consumers — do we need both edge.mjs and edge.cjs?

devon: Not really for middleware. Next Edge needs ESM. But other consumers (node servers) might import the same subpath; you can either ship both or document `@our/sdk/edge` as edge-only and keep the main entry for node.

rob: Also watch transitive deps. We had a tiny metrics lib that imported `node:crypto` and it snuck into the edge bundle. The solution was to provide a dev-time shim for the edge build: `alias 'metrics' -> './metrics-shim.js'` in esbuild/rollup.

ci-bot: build 1780123456 failed in staging: middleware import resolution mismatch. See https://ci.example/1780123456/logs

tasha: Great pointers. I'll run the resolve check, add the runtime guard, and pin a local lockfile for the staging job. Thanks! :sparkles:
